content:
We need to propose a retrosynthesis route (max 3 steps) to target molecule: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have some building blocks identified: maybe we can disconnect at sulfonamide bond (S(=O)2 attached to aniline). Also disconnect at amide bond linking the cinnamoyl anilide.

Goal: final product is a bis-aryl sulfonamide with a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to second phenyl with an aniline.

Potential disconnections:

1) Disconnection of sulfonamide: break S-N bond to give sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonic acid) and aniline. Template from earlier: Cl-[S](=O)(=O)-c... + NH2-aryl -> sulfonamide. So we can use sulfonyl chloride (aryl sulfonyl chloride) and aniline (aryl amine). So precursors: 4-methyl-2-? Actually the sulfonyl part is attached to phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2) which is para-substituted with the sulfonamide and the cinnamoyl amide side chain. The sulfonyl chloride would be 4-(C=... )-phenylsulfonyl chloride? Wait the sulfonyl chloride is attached to phenyl ring that also has the cinnamoyl amide substituent at para position relative to sulfonamide? In target: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the sulfonamide nitrogen attached to phenyl (c1ccc... ) is attached to sulfonyl group which is attached to second phenyl ring (c2). That second phenyl has the cinnamoyl amide substituent at para position relative to sulfonyl group. So the sulfonyl chloride precursor would be 4-(cinnamoyl amide) phenylsulfonyl chloride. That may be not commercially available. Alternative: we could first form the sulfonamide using sulfonyl chloride (aryl sulfonyl chloride) and aniline (the first phenyl with methyl). The aniline is Cc1ccc(NH2)cc1 (p-toluidine). That's commercially available (price 115). Good.

Now we need the sulfonyl chloride: 4-(C=C-C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N) phenylsulfonyl chloride. Could we get that via chlorosulfonation of the phenyl with the side chain? Might be expensive. Alternative route: first form the amide on the second phenyl (cinnamoyl anilide) then sulfonylate that phenyl to sulfonyl chloride then couple with p-toluidine. But we have max 3 steps total. So maybe step1: make the cinnamoyl anilide (intermediate A): c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 (i.e., 4-(E)-cinnamoyl anilide phenyl). This can be formed by amide coupling between 4-aminophenyl (p-aminophenyl) and trans-cinnamoyl chloride (or trans-cinnamic acid activated). Then step2: sulfonylate that phenyl with chlorosulfonic acid to give sulfonyl chloride (or directly sulfonyl chloride then couple with p-toluidine). But sulfonylation may be done after amide formation? The sulfonyl chloride is on the phenyl ring, not interfering with amide. So step2: treat the phenyl (with amide) with chlorosulfonic acid to give sulfonyl chloride (para to amide). Then step3: couple with p-toluidine to give sulfonamide.

Check availability of building blocks:

- p-toluidine (Cc1ccc(N)cc1) price 115 (or 28.6 for methyl aniline). Good.

- 4-aminophenyl (same as p-aminophenyl) is same as p-toluidine? Wait we need 4-aminophenyl without methyl. That's aniline with para amine? Actually we need phenyl with amine at para position to attach amide. The intermediate A is phenyl with amide at para position (C=...C(=O)N-Ph). Starting from 4-aminophenyl (aniline) we can acylate with trans-cinnamoyl chloride to give the amide. So we need 4-aminophenyl (aniline). That's just aniline (c1ccc(N)cc1). Search.
